source_tools.relevance: The reaction search was explicitly queried for N#CC>>NCC, the nitrile-to-amine connectivity change.
A second search queried CC#N>>CCN to screen empirical records for the same functional-group conversion.

key_findings.finding: The retrieved ORD records are not valid evidence for nitrile reduction: they predominantly show N-alkylation of a fluorinated heteroaromatic piperazine-like scaffold with acetonitrile or chloroacetonitrile, and retain the nitrile in the product. The reported 999.9% yields are anomalous and should be disregarded.

source_tools.relevance: Records 1–10 show CC#N or ClCH2CN incorporation into the heterocycle while the product still contains CC#N; water is listed as solvent and no reducing agent is present.
The repeated CC#N>>CCN search returned the same non-reduction records, confirming a database/index-match limitation.

key_findings.finding: Plausible literature-standard reagent systems for this transformation, subject to substrate compatibility testing, are catalytic hydrogenation (H2 with Raney Ni, Pd/C, or PtO2; commonly alcoholic solvent such as EtOH/MeOH, mild-to-moderate pressure), LiAlH4 in dry ether/THF followed by aqueous workup, or milder borane complexes (BH3·THF or BH3·SMe2). For preserving a fluorinated heteroaromatic scaffold, catalytic hydrogenation or borane is generally preferable to strongly reducing LiAlH4 when other reducible heteroaromatic functions are present; avoid conditions that can hydrogenolyze C–F or reduce the heteroaromatic ring. The available reaction-search records do not experimentally validate any of these systems for the supplied exact substrate.

source_tools.relevance: The reaction searches establish that the available matched records do not provide a valid reduction protocol for this substrate class; reagent recommendations beyond those records are standard chemical interpretation rather than retrieved empirical evidence.
